questions.question: A road mesh uses the usual back-face culling. It is visible from underneath but invisible from above. Which change to the mesh makes its triangles face upward?
answers: Point the vertex normals upward.
Swap two vertex indices within every triangle.
Reverse the order of the triangles, keeping each triangle’s vertex order.
Reverse the path, so the rungs run from its end back to its start.

questions.question: In Unity, a road’s tangent points in the direction of travel. Which calculation gives a direction toward the driver’s right?
answers: Cross world up with the tangent.
Cross the tangent with world up.
Use world right, the positive X axis.
Normalize the tangent.

questions.question: The generator adds two vertices per rung, left first, starting at rung 0. Quad i joins rung i to rung i + 1. Which vertex index is the quad’s top-left corner, the left vertex of rung i + 1?
On a road that climbs a hill, what goes wrong if every vertex normal is set to Vector3.up instead of being recalculated from the triangles?
answers: The slope is lit as if it were flat ground.
The road becomes invisible from above.
The texture stretches along the slope.
Nothing; up is correct on any road.

questions.question: A road’s rungs are placed at equal steps of the spline parameter u, and each rung moves the vertical texture coordinate v forward by the same amount. The road texture comes out squashed in some places and stretched in others. Which change makes it even?
answers: Use twice as many rungs.
Place the rungs at equal meters along the road, using the distance table.
Make the texture repeat less often.
Add extra rungs where the road bends.

questions.question: The generator uses Cross(world up, tangent).normalized for its sideways direction, with no fallback. The road stays full width on a 70-degree climb. At one rung, the tangent points exactly straight up. What happens to the width there?
answers: It stays full, because normalizing restores a unit sideways vector.
It stays full, but the left and right edges swap places.
It narrows, but the two edges stay apart.
It becomes zero: both edges meet at the centerline.
